enrichment.headline: Buys up to $2M in food from Sysco for student meals through Dec. 2021 without a public bid
enrichment.summary: The district is hiring Sysco San Francisco to supply extra meat, poultry, high-protein foods and fresh produce for its student meal program from August 12 to December 31, 2021. The district is skipping its own public bidding by using a legal exception to public bidding (called the Graydon exception). The contract is capped at $2,000,000.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Graydon Exception to Public Bidding and Nutrition Services Food Contract - Sysco San Francisco, Inc. - Chief Systems and Services Officer

enrichment.headline: Approves the 2021-22 summary of how Proposition 30 Education Protection Account funds will be spent
enrichment.summary: The board approves a resolution summarizing how the district will spend its Education Protection Account money (state funds from Proposition 30) in the 2021-22 fiscal year. The official text does not state a dollar amount.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Education Protection Act - Proposition 30 Funds - Fiscal Year 2021-2022

enrichment.headline: Allows temporary borrowing between district funds in 2021-22 to cover cash-flow needs
enrichment.summary: The board approves a resolution that lets the district borrow temporarily from one of its funds to another during the 2021-22 fiscal year when cash is short, and sets how the borrowed money is repaid. It cites Education Code Section 42603. No dollar amount is stated.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Temporary Borrowing Between District Funds - Fiscal Year 2021-2022

enrichment.headline: Approves the district's 2021-22 funding application to the state through the CARS system
enrichment.summary: The board approves the district's 2021-2022 application for funding through the state's Consolidated Application and Reporting System (CARS). It also authorizes the Superintendent, or a designee, to submit the application to the California Department of Education. No dollar amount is stated.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Consolidated Application and Reporting System (CARS) - Application for Funding - Fiscal Year 2021-2022 - Chief Business Officer

enrichment.headline: Asks Alameda County to set the tax rate for school bonds expected to be sold in 2021-22
enrichment.summary: The board adopts a resolution asking the Alameda County Board of Supervisors to set the property tax rate for Oakland Unified bonds that are expected to be sold during the 2021-22 fiscal year. It also authorizes the actions needed to carry this out. No dollar amount is stated.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: District General Obligation Bonds Sale - Fiscal Year 2021-2022 - Request to Board of Supervisors of the County of Alameda To Establish Tax Rate

enrichment.headline: Pays Consolidated Engineering Laboratories up to $36,367 for testing at Lincoln Elementary repairs
enrichment.summary: Consolidated Engineering Laboratories will provide materials testing and construction inspection for the water intrusion repairs at Lincoln Elementary School. The price is $26,367 for basic services plus $10,000 held for additional services if needed, for a cap of $36,367. Work was scheduled to start June 16, 2021, before this vote, and to run through August 23, 2021, though it may last longer if delays arise.

items.group: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
items.sourceIssue: The text calls the $10,000 contingency a 10% fee, but 10% of the $26,367.00 base amount would be about $2,637; the stated $36,367.00 total matches the $10,000 figure.
items.title: Agreement for Materials Testing Services – Consolidated Engineering Laboratories – Lincoln Elementary School Water Intrusion Repairs Project

enrichment.headline: Renews Brandman University partnership for teacher, counselor and psychologist interns through 2024
enrichment.summary: The district and Brandman University, a private nonprofit university, renew an agreement for intern and practicum placements. It covers K-12 teaching, education specialist, school counselor, clinical school psychologist and administrative services credentials, plus other student support credentials. It runs from July 1, 2021 to June 30, 2024. The text does not state a dollar amount.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Memorandum of Understanding and Interagency Agreement - District and Brandman University - Intern Partnership and Practica Programs - K-12 Teaching - Talent/Human Resources Department

enrichment.headline: Shares student data at no cost with Oakland Public Education Fund, Oakland REACH and two others
enrichment.summary: The district will share student-level data with The Oakland Public Education Fund, The Oakland REACH, CARES for Learning, and The New Teacher Project (TNTP). The groups will use it to understand students' earlier reading performance, track literacy growth and school engagement, keep families informed, and support families. The agreement covers April 21, 2021 to June 30, 2022 and costs the district nothing.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Data Sharing Agreement - The Oakland Public Education Fund, The Oakland REACH, CARES for Learning, and The New Teacher Project (TNTP) - Research, Assessment, and Data (RAD) Department

enrichment.headline: Updates the independent study policy (BP 6158) to match the new state law AB 130
enrichment.summary: The board adopts a resolution amending Board Policy 6158 on independent study (learning outside the regular classroom) so it lines up with AB 130, a state law enacted July 9, 2021. No dollar amount is stated.

items.fundingSource: Elementary and Secondary School Emergency Relief (ESSER) Act

outcome.action: Adopted

enrichment.headline: Adds $18,500 for Be The Change Consulting to run George Floyd Safety Plan design meetings
enrichment.summary: The board ratifies, meaning approves after the fact, a change that raises the contract with Be The Change Consulting from $30,000 to $48,500, an added $18,500. The firm facilitates process design team meetings for the George Floyd Safety Plan. The amendment covers April 1 to June 30, 2021, which was already over before this vote.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Amendment No.1, Professional Services Agreement 2020-2021 - Be The Change Consulting - Chief of Staff

enrichment.headline: Pays School Facility Consultants up to $190,000 to help win state school construction funding
enrichment.summary: School Facility Consultants will help the district work out and claim state funding eligibility for new school construction, modernization and joint-use projects. That includes preparing applications to the California Department of Education and the State Allocation Board. The contract is capped at $190,000 for July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
items.title: General Services Agreement – School Facility Consultants – Facilities Planning & Management Project - Division of Facilities Planning and Management

enrichment.headline: Extends Dialog Design's Madison Park Academy expansion contract by a year, with no added money
enrichment.summary: This amendment gives Dialog Design, LP (also known as Byrens Kim Design Works) 365 more days on its architectural services agreement for the Madison Park Academy Expansion Project. The end date moves from December 31, 2020 to December 30, 2021. The original agreement dates back to March 12, 2014. No money is added, and part of the added period came before this vote.

vendor.name: Dialog Design, LP (aka Byrens Kim Design Works)

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
items.title: Amendment No. 8, Architectural Services Agreement – Dialog Design, LP, aka Byrens Kim Design Works - Madison Park Academy Expansion Project - Division of Facilities Planning and Management

enrichment.headline: Awards Data Media Services $62,000 to install 25 security cameras at Oakland Tech and Melrose sites
enrichment.summary: Data Media Services, the lowest responsive bidder in a competitive bid, will install 25 exterior cameras and program the servers and software for the Video Surveillance Project. Sites include Oakland Technical High School and two Melrose Leadership Academy campuses. The $62,000 includes a $6,000 contingency. Work is expected to run 90 days, from August 12 to November 10, 2021.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
items.title: Agreement Between Owner and Contractor - Competitively Bid – Data Media Services, Inc. – Various Video Surveillance Project – Division of Facilities Planning & Management

enrichment.headline: Pays Xebec Data Corporation up to $4,000 to set up energy data exchange with PG&E
enrichment.summary: Xebec Data Corporation will set up and test an online data-exchange system so the district can send and receive energy-use data with PG&E, the utility, for the Prop 39 energy operations project. The agreement is capped at $4,000 and runs July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
items.title: General Services Agreement – Xebec Data Corporation – Prop 39 Energy Operations Facilities Planning & Management Project - Division of Facilities Planning and Management
